title: Compass · one question, the person's own identity, every system it touches
subtitle: Zava Credit Union · Teams → Agent Framework workflow → three Foundry agents → SharePoint and member data, as the signed-in person
summary: Compass is the trusted backend: it holds the person from Teams, performs one on-behalf-of exchange per downstream system, and hands the tokens to the agents the question needs, running in parallel. Foundry forwards them and never exchanges them. SharePoint and the member API decide what comes back — nothing is pruned in our code.
hopNote: the person's identity, in order from Teams sign-in to the store that enforces their permissions

detail.what: Credit officer. The first of the two people we sign in as.
detail.identity: His own Entra account; Teams SSO means no second sign-in.
detail.access: Reads the Lending Policy library, and the shared Member Services FAQ. Not the Portfolio and Collections library.
detail.managed: An existing tenant user (Copilot-licensed), reused from the earlier credit-memo build.

detail.what: Portfolio analyst, West. Asks the same questions from a different set of access.
detail.identity: Her own Entra account; a separate browser profile for the live demo.
detail.access: Reads Portfolio and Collections and the shared FAQ. Not the Lending Policy library.
detail.managed: An existing tenant user (Copilot-licensed), reused from the earlier credit-memo build.

detail.what: Admin-consents the bot's downstream delegated permissions so no employee is ever prompted.
detail.access: Graph Files.Read.All and Sites.Read.All, Azure AI Search user_impersonation, and the Zava API's Member.Read.
detail.notes: Done once, tenant-wide, for the bot app. Without it each person gets a consent prompt, which is exactly what we are avoiding.

detail.what: Where people talk to Compass.
detail.identity: Teams SSO issues a token for the bot's own API, silently.
detail.managed: Needs the Teams client IDs pre-authorized on the bot app, an OAuth connection with the Token Exchange URL, and webApplicationInfo in the app manifest.

detail.what: Searches SharePoint as the calling person and returns text extracts with their source URLs.
detail.identity: Called with the person's delegated Graph token, straight from x-client-graph-access-token.
detail.access: SharePoint's own permissions decide. Nothing comes back that the person could not already open, so nothing is pruned in our code.
detail.notes: Needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence per calling person. Semantic retrieval covers .docx, .pptx, .pdf, .aspx and .one; other types get lexical matching only.

detail.what: Three libraries with unique permissions: Lending Policy (Daniel), Portfolio and Collections (Maya), Member Services FAQ (both).
detail.access: Per-person permissions, enforced by SharePoint itself at query time. Neither route ever sees the ACL.
detail.notes: Permissions are SharePoint's, not the repo's. The demo's whole point: the same question returns different results, and the bot never needs to know why.

detail.what: The bot's Entra identity, and the client credential it uses for OBO.
detail.identity: A federated identity credential on the app registration trusts the bot's managed identity, so there is no secret to store or rotate.
detail.managed: Bot Service's OAuth connection credential is configured separately from this.

detail.what: What the bot authenticates to Azure and Foundry as.
detail.access: Holds the Foundry roles below. Also the subject of the federated credential, which is what removes the secret.

detail.what: Three access tokens the bot obtains on the person's behalf, one per audience.
detail.identity: Subject is the person; the bot is the actor.
detail.access: Each is good only for its own audience.
detail.notes: Foundry does not refresh them. Obtain them per turn and keep the turn inside their lifetime.

detail.what: Tenant-wide consent for the downstream scopes the bot requests as the person.
detail.access: Three grants on the bot app: Graph (Files.Read.All, Sites.Read.All), Azure AI Search (user_impersonation), Zava API (Member.Read).
detail.notes: Applied live to the sandbox tenant. Without it, the silent experience is impossible.

detail.what: Can require MFA or re-authentication part-way through a turn.
detail.access: A claims challenge must be carried back to the bot and satisfied through Teams sign-in.
detail.notes: Not exercised in the sandbox. Plan for it: an agent cannot resolve a challenge on its own.

detail.what: What lets the bot assert a person to a hosted agent.
detail.access: The Foundry role for calling agents, plus a custom role holding .../agents/endpoints/UserIdentityImpersonation/action.
detail.notes: The impersonation data action is in no built-in role. Without it, sending x-ms-user-identity is refused with 403. Today it is assigned at project scope; per-agent scope waits on a Foundry preview schema fix.

detail.what: Carries Teams activities to the bot and brokers the person's token for the bot's own API.
detail.identity: Brokers and stores; it does not issue downstream tokens. Entra does.
detail.notes: This is the service behind the engineering lead's question. The thing to ask for is Entra-native sign-in without the Bot Framework token service — not a replacement token service.

detail.what: Owns the conversation, authenticates the person, performs OBO, and calls Foundry with the person's tokens.
detail.identity: A confidential client. Learn's requirement is exactly this: a trusted application backend that authenticates users and can perform OBO.
detail.access: Scope its Foundry roles to what it must call, take the object ID only from a validated token, and give it no secret.
detail.notes: This is a trust boundary: the bot can assert any person to the agents its role covers.

detail.what: The bot exchanges the person's token for a downstream token, per audience, as a confidential client.
detail.identity: Entra issues every one of these. There is no second token service.
detail.notes: Compass already does this today for its function tools. The pattern does not change — only who it is handed to.

detail.what: A Microsoft Agent Framework workflow: scope the turn (the route, then the question) → the executors in scope in parallel → a fan-in barrier → compose one reply.
detail.identity: Receives the person and the three tokens once; never exchanges anything itself.
detail.access: Fail closed: if any branch fails the whole turn fails, and the original typed exception is rethrown.
detail.notes: A fresh workflow per turn, so no state or token can leak between people.

detail.what: Receives the bot's call and routes it to the agent that was asked for.
detail.identity: For hosted agents it forwards x-client-* to the container and drops the caller's Authorization header; it adds x-agent-user-id.
detail.access: Checks the bot's role and the impersonation action before accepting x-ms-user-identity.
detail.notes: Foundry does not exchange or refresh the token in x-client-*. End users need no Foundry role assignments in this pattern.

detail.what: Zava Credit Union's agent code, running as a hosted agent. Reads the person's Graph token from x-client-* and calls the Copilot Retrieval API as them.
detail.identity: Its own managed identity for platform concerns; the person's token for every data read.
detail.access: Never switches silently to app-only access: if a token is missing it makes no downstream call.
detail.managed: Deployed from a source zip (dotnet_10 runtime) using the Azure.AI.AgentServer.Responses adapter. No container registry.

detail.what: A prompt agent that answers from the Foundry IQ knowledge base. No container, no code of its own.
detail.identity: Receives the person's Search token as a structured input (search_auth_token) and passes it as x-ms-query-source-authorization on the knowledge-base call.
detail.access: The knowledge base's remote SharePoint source queries SharePoint as the person.
detail.notes: A prompt agent never sees x-client-* headers; the structured input is how the token reaches it. The model decides when to call the knowledge base.

detail.what: A hosted agent whose only job is Zava Credit Union's member data, over MCP.
detail.identity: Reads x-client-zava-api-token and passes it to the MCP server explicitly.
detail.access: The MCP server, not the agent, decides what this person may see.
detail.managed: Same source-zip deployment as the retrieval agent.

detail.what: Groups tools behind one MCP endpoint, with its own connection auth.
detail.identity: An oauth2 connection runs Foundry's own per-person authorization flow when no grant exists. Learn documents no way to hand it a token Compass already holds. user-entra-token is a different, platform-managed mechanism documented for Microsoft services.
detail.notes: This is what a toolbox OAuth connection does: a separate sign-in and consent in front of each MCP server, although Compass already had the person from Teams.

detail.what: Foundry's built-in SharePoint tool.
detail.notes: Learn is explicit: it “doesn't work when the agent is published to Microsoft Teams”. That rules it out for Compass.

detail.what: Letting Foundry publish the agent straight into Teams.
detail.notes: Not established for Zava Credit Union's no-new-prompt requirement. Pages describe delegation without documenting the full silent Teams-to-tool token path, and published agents don't support streaming responses or citations — both of which Compass uses.

detail.what: Ingest SharePoint into an Azure AI Search index and trim results at query time.
detail.identity: x-ms-query-source-authorization carries the person's token and Search trims by the ingested ACLs.
detail.notes: Permissions are as of the last sync, so a revoked person can still see content until the next run. The right choice for scale or semantic ranking over a large corpus; not for a permissions-sensitive, always-current answer. The SharePoint indexer and ACL ingestion are preview.

detail.what: A Foundry IQ knowledge base with a remote SharePoint knowledge source, hosted on Azure AI Search.
detail.identity: Takes the person's Search token and queries SharePoint live as them.
detail.access: SharePoint's permissions decide, with no copy of the content and no ACL snapshot.
detail.notes: Preview. Created by a script (Setup-KnowledgeBase). Slower per query than the Retrieval API, which is part of why route A is the default.

detail.what: Zava Credit Union's member tools, exposed as an MCP server on Azure Functions.
detail.identity: Validates audience and issuer of the person's token before doing anything.
detail.access: Receives the person's token from x-client-zava-api-token. Never forwards it to a different API — the MCP specification's rule.
detail.notes: Real server, simulated domain: member records live in SQLite. Seeded per person by Entra object id.

detail.what: Where the turn is traced.
detail.access: A redaction processor runs before the exporter, so no JWT-shaped string reaches telemetry.
detail.notes: Hosted agents do not yet emit telemetry of their own; that is a production gap, not a design choice.

detail.what: A simulated core-banking domain behind the MCP server. The identity path to it is real; the data is not.

steps.t: R1 · It has to answer as the person, not as the app
steps.x: The person is already in Teams. Their identity has to arrive at our code as something we can spend, without a second prompt.

steps.t: R2 · Act on their behalf, with no secret to leak
steps.x: The bot exchanges the person's token itself. Its credential is federated: the app registration trusts the managed identity, so nothing is stored or rotated.

steps.t: R3 · One token per system, never reused across audiences
steps.x: Graph, Search and our own API each get their own token, issued by Entra with the person as subject. A token for one audience is useless to the others.

steps.t: R4 · Carry the person through the agent platform without becoming the person
steps.x: Foundry takes the bot's own identity for authorization and the person's object id as a claim. The bot needs a role nobody gets by default, and Foundry still never exchanges the tokens.

steps.t: R5 · Let SharePoint decide what they may see — two routes
steps.x: Route A: a hosted agent calls the Copilot Retrieval API. Route B: a prompt agent calls a Foundry IQ knowledge base. Different plumbing, same rule: SharePoint's permissions decide.

steps.t: R6 · Reach our own data, over MCP, with the same person
steps.x: A third agent calls our MCP server with the Zava API token. The server validates audience and issuer, then resolves the person to a member.

steps.t: R7 · One reply from three answers, and fail closed
steps.x: An Agent Framework workflow fans out to the agents the question needs and waits at a fan-in barrier. If any branch fails, the whole turn fails — no partial answer, no silent downgrade.

steps.t: Daniel asks Compass in Teams
steps.x: He is already signed in. Nothing prompts him, and nothing will.

steps.t: Teams SSO hands the bot the person
steps.x: Bot Service brokers a token for the bot's own API. It brokers; it does not issue the downstream ones.

steps.t: The bot does the OBO once per system
steps.x: Graph, Search and the Zava API: three exchanges, all by Entra, all with Daniel as subject.

steps.t: The workflow fans out to the agents in scope
steps.x: Up to three calls in parallel, each carrying Daniel's object id and his tokens. Foundry forwards them and exchanges nothing.

steps.t: SharePoint decides, by two routes
steps.x: The Retrieval API and the knowledge base both query SharePoint as Daniel. He gets Lending Policy and the FAQ; Portfolio and Collections never comes back.

steps.t: Member data arrives scoped to him
steps.x: The MCP server validates the token and returns Daniel's member record, never Maya's.

steps.t: Maya asks the same question
steps.x: Same code, same agents, different tokens. She gets Portfolio and Collections and the FAQ, and not the Lending Policy. The bot never needed to know why.

scenarios.title: Two routes to the same SharePoint

steps.t: Route A · Copilot Retrieval API through a hosted agent
steps.x: The agent reads the Graph token from x-client-graph-access-token and calls the API as the person. Fast, and semantic over Office and PDF content.

steps.t: Route B · Foundry IQ knowledge base through a prompt agent
steps.x: The Search token rides as a structured input and becomes x-ms-query-source-authorization. The knowledge base queries SharePoint live as the person.

steps.t: Same permission model, different plumbing
steps.x: Neither route ever sees an ACL, and neither copies content. SharePoint decides at query time, so a revoked permission takes effect immediately.

steps.t: Why A is the default, and when you would choose B
steps.x: A is lower latency and GA. B is the right answer when the knowledge base should combine SharePoint with other sources, or when you want the model to plan its own sub-queries. An indexed source is for scale, at the cost of an ACL that is only as fresh as the last sync.

steps.t: Publish to Teams from Foundry
steps.x: Not established for a no-new-prompt requirement, and published agents support neither streaming nor citations — both of which Compass uses.

steps.t: The Foundry SharePoint tool
steps.x: Learn is explicit: it doesn't work when the agent is published to Microsoft Teams.

steps.t: A toolbox oauth2 connection
steps.x: Runs Foundry's own per-person authorization when no grant exists. No documented way to hand it the token Compass already holds.

steps.t: An indexed SharePoint source
steps.x: Permissions are as of the last sync. Fine at scale, wrong when the answer must always reflect who may see what right now.

scenarios.title: What has to be true before it works

steps.t: A federated credential instead of a secret
steps.x: The bot app registration trusts the bot's managed identity. Nothing to store, rotate or leak.

steps.t: An admin consents once, for everyone
steps.x: Three grants on the bot app, so no employee ever sees a consent prompt.

steps.t: The bot needs a role nobody gets by default
steps.x: The Foundry role to call agents plus a custom role holding the impersonation data action. Without it: 403 on every call.

steps.t: Conditional Access can still interrupt
steps.x: A claims challenge has to travel back to the bot and be satisfied in Teams. An agent cannot resolve it on its own.

steps.t: Traces without tokens
steps.x: Redaction runs before export, so no JWT-shaped string reaches Application Insights.
